name: Phaedrin
description: Phaedrin is Nightshade's entry into the fear-suppression market, but it takes a different approach than clinical amygdala blockers — instead of suppressing fear directly, it chemically induces a profound sense of calm acceptance, a neurological state that resembles the meditative dissociation described in certain contemplative traditions. Users report feeling entirely present, unhurried, and unafraid — not because danger feels unreal, but because the body's alarm response to danger has been decoupled from conscious experience. Nightshade markets it legally as an anxiety treatment.
effects: Profound calm and psychological stillness under threat
Suppression of panic response without cognitive impairment
Improved decision quality under extreme duress
Acceptance of physical risk without recklessness
side_effects: Dissociative detachment from emotional investment in outcomes
Users may fail to prioritize self-preservation appropriately
Mild euphoria that can interfere with urgency recognition
Post-dose period of emotional flatness lasting 4-6 hours
Psychological dependence develops quickly — users find undosed anxiety intolerable
Rare cases of users becoming too calm to act at all
cultural_context: Phaedrin occupies a strange cultural space in M88 — it is simultaneously a legitimate anxiety medication prescribed to Tier 3 office workers and a combat drug favored by a particular type of professional: the deliberate, experienced runner who has been doing this long enough that they don't need aggression, just stillness. In Shelf combat culture it is called 'Ghost Dose' because people on Phaedrin move through danger with an eerie unhurried quality. There is a small quasi-spiritual subculture around it that Nightshade finds both useful for marketing and mildly unsettling.
story_hooks: A Phaedrin-dependent runner has been offered a job she knows she should turn down — but her chemically induced calm keeps telling her it's fine, and she can't tell anymore if that's wisdom or the drug.

Nightshade's Phaedrin prescriptions are being written in enormous quantities by a single clinic in Tier 2 — the clinic is a front, and the drug is being bulk-diverted somewhere, but the destination is unclear.
A runner encounters an enemy combatant on Phaedrin during an op — the woman is calm, unhurried, and utterly unafraid, which is more frightening than any berserker compound would be.
